rules.rationale: Explicit source value prior: smiles_short had positive solubility effect; small solutes pay a low cavity-formation cost in water.
Largest-magnitude source prior was negative for smiles_long; bulky hydrophobic solutes desolvate poorly.
Ring role carried the highest transfer weight (0.758); rigid ring systems reduced solubility in source data.
Rotatable-bond role maps to branching with transfer weight 0.758; limited flexibility lowers entropic desolvation penalty.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers ESOL size, ring and branching effects to hydration ranking. Fails because aqueous solubility mixes crystal-lattice terms absent from pure hydration free energy, and source role confidences are only 0.16-0.41.

rules.rationale: Dense N/O centers donate and accept hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Broader-coverage polar tier; some hydrogen-bonding capacity still offsets cavity-formation cost in water.
Pure hydrocarbons offer neither hydrogen bonding nor polarizable halogens, so cavity cost is uncompensated.
Counter-hypothesis reversing the weakly supported negative smiles_mid source prior; moderate size accommodates more polar groups.

skills.hypothesis: Hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding capacity rather than molecular size, reversing the mid-length source penalty. Fails if the score rewards small apolar solutes or if hetero_high coverage (28 items) is unrepresentative.

lesson: Source ESOL roles are size- and ring-dominated with low confidence (0.16-0.41), while hydration free energy is mechanistically governed by polar hydrogen bonding; prefer the mechanism-first prior, broaden it beyond thin bins, and decay semantic mass so revealed target data can override it.
